gap: No result ChatGPT got states a bench-measured capacity for any LiFePO4 battery. Techtest.org (Michael Barton) discharged the three 12V 100Ah candidates with an electronic load and got 1,378 Wh / 107.7 Ah for the Redodo, 1,321 to 1,368 Wh / about 105.5 Ah for the Power Queen and 1,289 to 1,316 Wh / about 102 Ah for the ECO-Worthy. The rating for all three is 1,280 Wh. After about a year of daily solar cycling, the Power Queen kept about 102 Ah (roughly 3% lost) and the ECO-Worthy fell to 97 Ah (roughly 5% lost).
standout_why: I opened the Bixpower 20Ah + charger kit page (bixpower.com/product-p/bat-lf1220-sp60w.htm). It gives only maker specs: 256 Wh, a 14.6 V 6 A charger, 'less than 4 hours', 2,000 cycles. It has no measured figures. The Dakota Lithium product pages, the Chameleon kit page and the epowerguys page all returned HTTP 429, so I could not read them. Their titles and search snippets show retailer or maker listings, and the search I ran turned up no bench test of the Powerbox 10 (Wired2Fish only repeats the maker's 'iPhone 11+ times' claim). ChatGPT's answer is a generic voltage/charger table with three Amazon-style cards and no measured number. None of the 13 results is a test page.
decides: This supports the 12V 100Ah picks: all three 100Ah brands measured above their 1,280 Wh rating, so the shopper is not paying for missing capacity. It ranks them on measured energy as Redodo (1,378 Wh) > Power Queen (1,321 to 1,368 Wh) > ECO-Worthy (1,289 to 1,316 Wh). On a one-year re-test of one unit each, Power Queen held capacity better than ECO-Worthy (3% vs 5% loss). The measurements alone do not decide the pick, for two reasons. The tested units are not the exact variants on our page: the Redodo test was the plain 12V 100Ah, not the low-temp trolling or self-heating version; the Power Queen test was the self-heating version, not the Low-Temp kit; and the ECO-Worthy test was a 2021 non-Bluetooth unit with no low-temp cutoff. Also, every test uses a single sample.
